families.ch01: One cream lander keeps its folded right leg. A single broad natural rock bears beneath a sound lower crossmember; no metal crib or repaired leg appears. Independently patch and pressurize the adjacent rounded habitat.
families.ch05: Imported cream and mustard press visibly includes a pressing chamber and twin hot-working rollers. Factory receiver unfolds on its own tracking feet; imported mirror petals complete the solar furnace. No locally fabricated metal bootstrap or workshop building.
families.ch07: Low two-course ceramic deck continuously supported on the floor, not thin ceramic rails or metal-legged furniture. Separate silver insulation and thin foldable cream mattress retain the deck footprint in either order.
families.ch08: Three broad ceramic troughs on solid plinths, with cream folded liners and elevated drain ports. Distinct bare, lined, loose-hose, reservoir-only and connected states. Three hoses descend to a common collector above a low dry imported basin and pump. Leave floor between objects transparent.
families.ch09: Same lined ceramic troughs, first empty then filled with tan porous root medium. A separate hose connects the left wall freshwater tap to the reservoir side; the three crop drains retain their independent common return.
families.ch10: Three independent zones in the same ceramic farm: left dark potato wrap then leafy shoots, back soybean seedlings, right pale wicking fabric then young lettuce. Retain ceramic walls, established drains, low reservoir and pump.
families.ch11: Established ceramic farm and a separate right-wall food sink; food washing never takes place in the nutrient reservoir.
families.ch12: Raise a dark fabric collar above the left ceramic bed rim, then add medium around lower potato stems while foliage remains exposed. A separate stake-and-string trellis supports the back soybean row. Lettuce and the shared drainage stay in place.
families.ch19: The left pale factory footing receives expansion solar modules; a separate right ceramic pad receives a simple open bolted steel process frame. Plain angles, flat gussets and accessible fasteners, not a factory casting.
families.ch21: Three distinct imported machines outdoors: left solar dish with removable sealed hydrogen-fed retort, separate square electric refining furnace with refractory crucible, and cream press with rollers. Gas hose leads left toward its dedicated source. No process frame appears before its later construction.
families.ch23: The same retort leaves the solar seat and enters the previously constructed open steel frame. Keep the dish's empty seat valid, preserve the press/rollers and separate refining furnace, and route the hydrogen feed toward the dedicated source rather than the press.
families.ch28: The established ceramic farm gains a rear cloth screen, a flexible wrinkled cream reservoir cover with return/vent openings, then quilted silver side insulation. Cover is sheet material, not a rigid steel lid. Freshwater feed and crop drains remain separate.
families.ch30: The same rock remains loaded while adjacent ground is graded, a two-course ceramic footing is laid, and a simple bolted X-braced steel support is fitted. Only the final load-transfer state levels the cabin and rolls the rock clear; original faulty leg remains.
families.ch31: Level lander retains the completed X-braced steel support on its ceramic footing. Separate blue methane and silver oxygen lines enter distinct cabin ports; either or both can be fitted on the same registered canvas.
families.ch32: Return to the established solar furnace, retaining the press's visible rolling attachment. Cooking uses the real imported pressure vessel and locally made conducting jacket.
families.ch33: Harvest-ready yellowing potato foliage, dry soybean pods on the existing trellis and fresh green lettuce remain in the ceramic beds. Preserve the taller potato collar, rear screen, flexible reservoir cover, side insulation and distinct feed/return hoses. Food sink remains separate.

items.rock: Broad irregular rust-red natural stone, traced from the actual selected lander support; fractured surface and gently flattened top, not a manufactured brick or steel lump.
items.steel-pin: One smooth low-carbon clevis pin with a broad head and transverse end hole, scavenged from an expendable restraint. Small individual object, not a renewable supply of steel.
items.separator-electromagnet: The same visible pin with insulated copper winding over a pale insulating sleeve and two short insulated leads. Pin head and end hole retain identity; no horseshoe permanent magnet or fabricated steel core.
items.carbon-and-flux: Two compact supplied cups: dark carbon pieces and pale granular flux. Symbolic small processing charges; exact chemistry is conveyed by name and reading, not colour alone.
items.iron-refining-charge: Dark refractory crucible with a handling ring and coarse porous iron/mineral charge plus flux. Distinct from loose sponge and from the solid finished billet; grade and refining stage require context.
items.steel-billet: One solid plain rectangular dark-grey billet with a lightly oxidized surface and squared ends, visibly consolidated rather than loose ore or porous sponge. Composition is stated in the reading.
items.steel: Compact representative bars and sheet, reusing the suitable existing 44-pixel stock symbol. It denotes checked local batch output, not recovered shipping braces or a literal pile of unlimited mass.
items.tool-kit: Existing compact 44-pixel symbol for the supplied working tools. The illustrated implements represent the kit, not its exhaustive inventory; no tool primitive occurs in the first two chapters.
items.survey-excavator-without-a-hopper: Same imported cream/mustard tracked excavator and toothed drum; hinged hopper panels folded flat at the rear, with retaining bolts, no empty bare chassis. Power connector loose.
items.powered-excavator-without-a-hopper: Same folded-hopper excavator; green instrument light distinguishes powered preparation, drum stationary. Do not imply that the hopper has been built from local steel. The reading supplies connection state where the small indicator is inconclusive.
items.furnace-receiver: Integrated imported cream insulated cylindrical receiver and its own low teal tracking cradle, hinged feet and empty petal sockets. No optical petals until assembly. Exact solar purpose requires the chapter context.
items.unseated-antenna: Reuse the existing intact straight dish with its hand mounting hardware. It has become detached, not bent or broken; hand latches restore it to its existing outdoor mount.
